title: All’s Fair Premiere Shines at Rome Film Festival 2026: Kardashian, Jenner, Watts & Stars Walk Red Carpet
body:
The glittering streets of Rome played host to a star‑studded showcase on Tuesday as the opening night of the Rome Film Festival’s 2026 lineup unfolded on the historic Via Veneto. Among the glittering silhouettes on the red carpet were reality‑TV mogul Kim Kardashian, matriarch Kris Jenner, Academy‑Award‑winning actress Naomi Watts and a host of international talent, all gathering to celebrate the world premiere of “All’s Fair,” the festival’s most anticipated drama of the season.

The event, which marked the festival’s 31st edition, turned the ancient capital into a runway of haute couture and celebrity flair. Kardashian arrived in a custom‑designed, sequined sheath dress by Balmain, paired with a sleek, low‑cut blazer that highlighted her signature glam aesthetic. Jenner, ever the fashion chameleon, opted for a bold, emerald‑green Valentino gown with a dramatic train, while Watts chose a classic, understated black silk number that let her performance‑oriented reputation shine through. Photographers captured the trio side by side, underscoring the cross‑generational appeal of the festival and hinting at the diverse audience the film hopes to attract.

“All’s Fair,” directed by emerging auteur Luca Moretti, is a contemporary retelling of the classic “fair‑play” myth set against the backdrop of modern politics and media manipulation. The narrative follows a charismatic media strategist who orchestrates a high‑stakes political campaign, blurring the lines between truth and spectacle. The film’s casting—featuring Hollywood veterans alongside rising European stars—mirrors its thematic concerns about the collision of old‑world values with new‑era digital influence. The presence of Kardashian, whose own brand is built on media savvy, and Jenner, a seasoned manager of celebrity narratives, added an extra layer of meta‑commentary to the proceedings.

Industry insiders noted that the festival’s decision to spotlight “All’s Fair” reflects a broader shift in European festivals toward programming that tackles contemporary sociopolitical issues through a cinematic lens. Rome’s selection committee, chaired by veteran director Sofia Coppola, emphasized the film’s relevance to current debates about misinformation, electoral integrity and the power of personal branding. “We are looking for stories that resonate beyond the screen, that provoke conversation in the streets of Rome and beyond,” Coppola said in a pre‑screening interview. The film’s premiere was followed by a lively Q&A session, during which director Moretti discussed his inspiration drawn from the 2020s’ “post‑truth” era, citing both American reality television and European political scandals as key influences.

The red‑carpet buzz extended beyond the main cast, with notable appearances by Italian cinema legend Monica Bellucci, French indie darling Léa Seydoux, and South Korean pop icon IU, whose presence highlighted the festival’s increasingly global outlook. Fashion houses capitalized on the exposure, unveiling limited‑edition collaborations and showcasing sustainable fabrics—a nod to Rome’s growing commitment to eco‑conscious event planning. Moreover, the festival’s digital platform streamed the opening night to over 20 million viewers worldwide, marking a record for simultaneous online engagement and underscoring the event’s hybrid model of in‑person and virtual participation.

As the lights dimmed and “All’s Fair” rolled onto the silver screen, the audience responded with a mixture of applause and thoughtful silence, suggesting that the film’s provocative themes struck a chord. Critics in the front rows praised the tight screenplay and nuanced performances, while others hinted that the film’s ambition might outpace its execution. Nonetheless, the consensus was clear: the movie has ignited a conversation that will likely ripple through both the festival circuit and the broader cultural discourse.

Looking ahead, the Rome Film Festival’s 2026 edition promises to continue its tradition of blending artistic excellence with timely social commentary. With “All’s Fair” setting a high bar for narrative relevance, upcoming selections—including a documentary on climate refugees and a sci‑fi thriller exploring AI ethics—are poised to keep audiences engaged and debating long after the final credits roll. The festival’s ability to attract high‑profile personalities while championing thought‑provoking cinema suggests that Rome will remain a pivotal hub for global storytelling in the years to come.
